from anonymous_definition import audit_anonymous_definition
from audit_dangerous_triggers import audit_dangerous_triggers
from output_format import format_github, format_sarif

VERSION = "1.25.2"


def collect(inputs, kinds, strict=False):
    items = []
    for given in inputs:
        if given == "-":
            text = sys.stdin.read()
            if not text.strip():
                continue
            if re.search(r"(?m)^version\s*:\s*2\s*$", text) and re.search(r"(?m)^updates\s*:", text):
                typ = "dependabot"
            elif re.search(r"(?m)^runs\s*:", text):
                typ = "actions"
            elif re.search(r"(?m)^jobs\s*:", text):
                typ = "workflows"
            else:
                continue
            if typ in kinds or "all" in kinds or "default" in kinds:
                items.append(("<stdin>", text, typ))
            continue
        p = Path(given)
        if p.is_dir():
            if "all" in kinds or "default" in kinds or "workflows" in kinds:
                wf = p / ".github" / "workflows"
                if wf.is_dir():
                    items.extend((str(f), f.read_text(errors="replace"), "workflows")
                                 for f in sorted(wf.rglob("*.yml")) + sorted(wf.rglob("*.yaml")))
            if "all" in kinds or "default" in kinds or "actions" in kinds:
                for pat in ("action.yml", "action.yaml"):
                    items.extend((str(f), f.read_text(errors="replace"), "actions")
                                 for f in sorted(p.rglob(pat)))
            if "all" in kinds or "default" in kinds or "dependabot" in kinds:
                for f in (p / ".github" / "dependabot.yml", p / ".github" / "dependabot.yaml"):
                    if f.is_file():
                        items.append((str(f), f.read_text(errors="replace"), "dependabot"))
            continue
        if not p.exists():
            raise FileNotFoundError(given)
        text = p.read_text(errors="replace")
        typ = "dependabot" if "dependabot" in p.name.lower() else "actions" if p.name.startswith("action.") else "workflows"
        # Match collection's useful minimum schema check, preventing arbitrary
        # YAML and empty files from being treated as valid inputs.
        if not (re.search(r"(?m)^jobs\s*:", text) or
                re.search(r"(?m)^runs\s*:", text) or
                (re.search(r"(?m)^version\s*:\s*2\s*$", text) and
                 re.search(r"(?m)^updates\s*:", text))):
            if strict:
                raise ValueError(f"invalid input: {given}")
            print(f" WARN collect_inputs: failed to validate {given} as input", file=sys.stderr)
            continue
        items.append((str(p), text, typ))
    return items


def audit_file(path, text, persona):
    findings = []
    # The available rules apply primarily to workflow and action YAML.
    findings += audit_uses(text, path, persona.capitalize())
    findings += audit_dangerous_triggers(text, path, persona)
    findings += audit_insecure_commands(text, path, persona.capitalize())
    findings += audit_bot_conditions(text, path, persona.capitalize())
    findings += audit_excessive_permissions(text, path, persona.capitalize())
    if persona in ("pedantic", "auditor"):
        findings += audit_anonymous_definition(text, path, persona)
    return findings


def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="zizmor", description="Static analysis for GitHub Actions")
    ap.add_argument("inputs", nargs="*")
    ap.add_argument("--collect", action="append", default=[])
    ap.add_argument("--strict-collection", action="store_true")

    ap.add_argument("--no-ignores", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("-v", "--verbose", action="count", default=0)
    ap.add_argument("-q", "--quiet", action="count", default=0)
    ap.add_argument("--format", choices=["plain", "json", "json-v1", "sarif", "github"], default="plain")
    ap.add_argument("--no-progress", action="store_true")

## `template-injection`

| Type     | Examples                 | Introduced in | Works offline  | Auto-fixes available | Configurable |
|----------|--------------------------|---------------|----------------|--------------------| ---------------|
| Workflow, Action  | [template-injection.yml] | v0.1.0        | ✅             | ✅        | ❌  |

[template-injection.yml]: https://github.com/woodruffw/gha-hazmat/blob/main/.github/workflows/template-injection.yml

Detects potential sources of code injection via template expansion.

GitHub Actions allows workflows to define *template expansions*, which
occur within special `${{ ... }}` delimiters. These expansions happen
before workflow and job execution, meaning the expansion
of a given expression appears verbatim in whatever context it was performed in.

Template expansions aren't syntax-aware, meaning that they can result in
unintended shell injection vectors. This is especially true when they're
used with attacker-controllable expression contexts, such as
`github.event.issue.title` (which the attacker can fully control by supplying
a new issue title).

!!! tip

    When used with a "pedantic" or "auditor"
    [persona](./usage.md#using-personas), this audit will flag *all* template
    expansions in code contexts, even ones that are likely safe.

    This is because `zizmor` considers all template expansions in code contexts
    to be code smells, and attempting to selectively permit them is more
    error-prone than forbidding them in a blanket fashion.

Other resources:

* [Keeping your GitHub Actions and workflows secure Part 2: Untrusted input]

### Remediation

The most common forms of template injection are in `run:` and similar
code-execution blocks. In these cases, an inline template expansion
can typically be replaced by an environment variable whose value comes
from the expanded template.

This avoids the vulnerability, since variable expansion is subject to normal
shell quoting/expansion rules.

!!! tip

    To fully remediate the vulnerability, you **should not** use
    `${{ env.VARNAME }}`, since that is still a template expansion.
    Instead, you should use `${VARNAME}` to ensure that the shell *itself*
    performs the variable expansion.


!!! tip

    When switching to `${VARNAME}`, keep in mind that different shells have
    different environment variable syntaxes. In particular, Powershell (the
    default shell on Windows runners) uses `${env:VARNAME}`.

    To avoid having to specialize your handling for different runners,
    you can set `#!yaml shell: sh` or `#!yaml shell: bash`.

!!! example

    === "Before :warning:"

        ```yaml title="template-injection.yml" hl_lines="3"
        - name: Check title
          run: |
            title="${{ github.event.issue.title }}"
            if [[ ! $title =~ ^.*:\ .*$ ]]; then
              echo "Bad issue title"
              exit 1
            fi
        ```

    === "After :white_check_mark:"

        ```yaml title="template-injection.yml" hl_lines="3 8-9"
        - name: Check title
          run: |
            title="${ISSUE_TITLE}"
            if [[ ! $title =~ ^.*:\ .*$ ]]; then
              echo "Bad issue title"
              exit 1
            fi
          env:
            ISSUE_TITLE: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
        ```

const p="*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: /workspace/audit_template_injection.py
+"""Basic workflow template-injection detection for shell run blocks."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import os
+import re
+
+from finding import finding, finding_location
+
+
+_EXPR = re.compile(r"\$\{\{\s*(.*?)\s*\}\}")
+
+
+def _risk(expr: str, persona: str):
+    if persona in ("pedantic", "auditor"):
+        return "High", "High"
+    e = expr.strip()
+    if e.startswith(("github.event.", "github.ref", "github.actor", "github.head_ref", "github.base_ref")):
+        return "High", "High"
+    if e.startswith("inputs."):
+        return "Low", "Low"
+    if e.startswith("vars."):
+        return "Informational", "Low"
+    if e.startswith(("secrets.", "matrix.", "strategy.")):
+        return None
+    return None
+
+
+def audit_template_injection(text: str, filename: str, persona: str = "regular") -> list[dict]:
+    lines = text.splitlines(keepends=True)
+    offsets = []
+    off = 0
+    for line in lines:
+        offsets.append(off)
+        off += len(line.encode("utf-8"))
+    path = os.path.abspath(filename)
+    out = []
+    job = None
+    steps_indent = None
+    step_index = -1
+    i = 0
+    while i < len(lines):
+        line = lines[i].rstrip("\r\n")
+        indent = len(line) - len(line.lstrip())
+        stripped = line.strip()
+        if indent == 2 and stripped.endswith(":") and not stripped.startswith("-"):
+            job = stripped[:-1].strip("'\"")
+            steps_indent = None
+            step_index = -1
+        if job is not None and stripped == "steps:":
+            steps_indent = indent
+            step_index = -1
+        if steps_indent is not None and indent > steps_indent and stripped.startswith("-"):
+            step_index += 1
+            step_indent = indent
+            step_start_line = i
+            # Tree-sitter's step node starts after the YAML list marker.
+            key_offset = offsets[i] + len(line[:line.find("-") + 1].encode("utf-8"))
+            j = i
+            while j + 1 < len(lines):
+                nxt = lines[j + 1].rstrip("\r\n")
+                if nxt.strip() and len(nxt) - len(nxt.lstrip()) <= step_indent:
+                    break
+                j += 1
+            step_end = offsets[j] + len(lines[j].rstrip("\r\n").encode("utf-8"))
+            step_text = text.encode("utf-8")[key_offset:step_end].decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
+            # Find run scalar key in this step. Block scalars include the `|`
+            # marker and all indented script lines as their source feature.
+            run_line = None
+            for k in range(i, j + 1):
+                if re.match(r"^\s+run\s*:", lines[k]):
+                    run_line = k
+                    break
+            if run_line is not None:
+                raw = lines[run_line].rstrip("\r\n")
+                colon = raw.find(":")
+                value_start_col = colon + 1
+                while value_start_col < len(raw) and raw[value_start_col] == " ":
+                    value_start_col += 1
+                value = raw[value_start_col:]
+                run_end_line = run_line
+                if value in ("|", "|-", "|+", ">", ">-", ">+"):
+                    for k in range(run_line + 1, j + 1):
+                        nxt = lines[k].rstrip("\r\n")
+                        if nxt.strip() and len(nxt) - len(nxt.lstrip()) <= len(raw) - len(raw.lstrip()):
+                            break
+                        run_end_line = k
+                run_start = offsets[run_line] + len(raw[:value_start_col].encode("utf-8"))
+                run_end = offsets[run_end_line] + len(lines[run_end_line].rstrip("\r\n").encode("utf-8"))
+                run_text = text.encode("utf-8")[run_start:run_end].decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
+                for match in _EXPR.finditer(run_text):
+                    expr = match.group(1)
+                    levels = _risk(expr, persona)
+                    if levels is None:
+                        continue
+                    severity, confidence = levels
+                    expr_start = run_start + len(run_text[:match.start(1)].encode("utf-8"))
+                    expr_end = expr_start + len(expr.encode("utf-8"))
+                    hidden = finding_location(path, "this step", ["jobs", job, "steps", step_index], text, key_offset, step_end, kind="Hidden")
+                    primary = finding_location(path, "may expand into attacker-controllable code", ["jobs", job, "steps", step_index, "run"], text, expr_start, expr_end,
+                                               feature_kind={"Subfeature": {"after": 0, "fragment": {"Raw": expr}}})
+                    primary["concrete"]["feature"] = run_text
+                    out.append(finding("template-injection", "code injection via template expansion", severity, confidence, persona.capitalize(), [hidden, primary]))
+        i += 1
+    return out
+
*** End Patch";
const r=await tools.apply_patch(p);text(r)

## `self-hosted-runner`

| Type     | Examples            | Introduced in | Works offline  | Auto-fixes available | Configurable |
|----------|---------------------|---------------|----------------|--------------------| ---------------|
| Workflow  | [self-hosted.yml] | v0.1.0        | ✅             | ❌                 | ❌  |

[self-hosted.yml]: https://github.com/woodruffw/gha-hazmat/blob/main/.github/workflows/self-hosted.yml

!!! note

    This is a `--pedantic` only audit, due to `zizmor`'s limited ability
    to analyze runner configurations themselves. See #34 for more details.

Detects self-hosted runner usage within workflows.

GitHub supports self-hosted runners, which behave similarly to GitHub-hosted
runners but use client-managed compute resources.

Self-hosted runners are very hard to secure by default, which is why
GitHub does not recommend their use in public repositories.

Other resources:

* [Self-hosted runner security]

### Remediation

In general, self-hosted runners should only be used on private repositories.
Exposing self-hosted runners to potential public use is *always* a security
risk.

In practice, there are many cases (such as custom host configurations) where
a self-hosted runner is needed on a public repository. In these cases,
there are steps you can take to minimize their risk:

1. Require manual approval on workflows for all external contributors.
   This can be configured at repository, workflow, or enterprise-wide
   levels. See [GitHub's docs] for more information.
1. Use only [ephemeral ("just-in-time") runners]. These runners are
   created just-in-time to perform one job and are destroyed immediately
   afterwards, making it harder (but not impossible) for an attacker to
   maintain persistence.

[GitHub's docs]: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/managing-workflow-runs-and-deployments/managing-workflow-runs/approving-workflow-runs-from-public-forks

[ephemeral ("just-in-time") runners]: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions#using-just-in-time-runners

## `stale-action-refs`

| Type     | Examples                | Introduced in | Works offline  | Auto-fixes available | Configurable |
|----------|-------------------------|---------------|----------------|--------------------|--------------|
| Workflow, Action  | N/A            | v1.7.0        | ❌            | ❌                | ❌          |

Checks for `#!yaml uses:` clauses which pin an action using a SHA reference,
but where that reference does not point to a Git tag.

When using an action commit which is not a Git tag / release version, that commit
might contain bugs or vulnerabilities which have not been publicly documented
because they might have been fixed before the subsequent release. Additionally,
because changelogs are usually only published for releases, it is difficult to
tell which changes of the subsequent release the pinned commit includes.

!!! note

    This is a `--pedantic` only audit because the detected situation is not
    a vulnerability per se. But it might be worth investigating which commit
    the SHA reference points to, and why not a SHA reference pointing to a
    Git tag is used.

    Some action repositories use a "rolling release branch" strategy where
    all commits on a certain branch are considered releases. In such a case
    findings of this audit can likely be ignored.

## `secrets-inherit`

| Type     | Examples                | Introduced in | Works offline  | Auto-fixes available | Configurable |
|----------|-------------------------|---------------|----------------|--------------------| ---------------|
| Workflow  | [secrets-inherit.yml]   | v1.1.0      | ✅             | ❌                 | ❌  |

[secrets-inherit.yml]: https://github.com/woodruffw/gha-hazmat/blob/main/.github/workflows/secrets-inherit.yml

Detects excessive secret inheritance between calling workflows and reusable
(called) workflows.

[Reusable workflows] can be given secrets by their calling workflow either
explicitly, or in a blanket fashion with `#!yaml secrets: inherit`. The latter
should almost never be used, as it makes it violates the
[Principle of Least Authority] and makes it impossible to determine which exact
secrets a reusable workflow was executed with.

### Remediation

In general, `#!yaml secrets: inherit` should be replaced with a `#!yaml secrets:` block
that explicitly forwards each secret actually needed by the reusable workflow.

!!! example

    === "Before :warning:"

        ```yaml title="reusable.yml" hl_lines="4"
        jobs:
          pass-secrets-to-workflow:
            uses: ./.github/workflows/called-workflow.yml
            secrets: inherit
        ```

    === "After :white_check_mark:"

        ```yaml title="reusable.yml" hl_lines="4-6"
        jobs:
          pass-secrets-to-workflow:
            uses: ./.github/workflows/called-workflow.yml
            secrets:
              forward-me: ${{ secrets.forward-me }}
              me-too: ${{ secrets.me-too }}
        ```

## `secrets-outside-env`

| Type     | Examples                | Introduced in | Works offline  | Auto-fixes available | Configurable |
|----------|-------------------------|---------------|----------------|--------------------| ---------------|
| Workflow  | [secrets-outside-env.yml]   | v1.23.0      | ✅             | ❌                 | ❌  |

[secrets-outside-env.yml]: https://github.com/zizmorcore/zizmor/blob/main/crates/zizmor/tests/integration/test-data/secrets-outside-env.yml

Detects usage of the `secrets` context in jobs without a dedicated environment.

GitHub Actions allows secrets to be configured at the organization, repository,
or environment level. The first two of these expose the configured secrets
to an entire repository (or repositories), while the last one allows secrets to be
scoped to specific conditions *within* a repository, as defined by the
environment's [protection rules].

[protection rules]: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/deploy/configure-and-manage-deployments/manage-environments#creating-an-environment

Consequently, configuring secrets at the environment level ensures that they're
only exposed to jobs that meet the environment's protection rules, mitigating
the risk of secrets being exposed to untrusted code or compromised workflows.

!!! tip

    The `secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN` secret is a special case, and is not flagged
    by this audit. This is because the permissions of the `GITHUB_TOKEN`
    secret are entirely determined by the workflow and job-level permissions.

"""Source-based template injection audit for GitHub Actions code fields."""
import re
from finding import finding, finding_location

UNTRUSTED = re.compile(r"github\.event\.(?:issue\.(?:title|body)|pull_request\.(?:title|body)|comment\.(?:body)|review\.(?:body)|discussion\.(?:title|body))", re.I)
EXPR = re.compile(r"\$\{\{\s*(.*?)\s*\}\}")


def audit_template_injection(text: str, filename: str, persona: str = "Regular") -> list[dict]:
    lines = text.splitlines(keepends=True)
    offsets, off = [], 0
    for line in lines:
        offsets.append(off); off += len(line)
    jobs = []
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        jm = re.match(r"^\s{2}([^\s#][^:]*):\s*(?:#.*)?$", line.rstrip("\r\n"))
        if jm:
            jobs.append((i, jm.group(1).strip().strip("'\"")))
    results = []
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        # run: and script-like code contexts are analyzed; inline expressions
        # in env/with values do not execute as code directly.
        key = re.match(r"^(\s*)(?:-\s*)?(run|script|inlineScript)\s*:\s*(.*?)(?:\r?\n)?$", line, re.I)
        if not key:
            continue
        indent = len(key.group(1))
        jobpair = next(((n, name) for n, name in reversed(jobs) if n < i), None)
        if not jobpair:
            continue
        job_i, job = jobpair
        step_i = next((k for k in range(i, job_i, -1) if re.match(r"^\s{6}-\s+", lines[k])), None)
        job_route = ["jobs", job]
        if step_i is not None:
            step_indent = len(lines[step_i]) - len(lines[step_i].lstrip())
            index = sum(1 for k in range(job_i + 1, step_i + 1)
                        if re.match(r"^\s{%d}-\s+" % step_indent, lines[k])) - 1
            route = job_route + ["steps", index]
        else:
            route = job_route
        code_start_line = i
        code_end_line = i + 1
        if key.group(3).strip() in ("|", ">", "|-", ">-") or not key.group(3).strip():
            while code_end_line < len(lines):
                s = lines[code_end_line].rstrip("\r\n")
                if s.strip() and len(s) - len(s.lstrip()) <= indent:
                    break
                code_end_line += 1
        code_start = offsets[code_start_line] + key.start(2)
        code_end = offsets[code_end_line] if code_end_line < len(lines) else len(text)
        # Find expressions in source lines inside the code field.
        matches = []
        for row in range(i, code_end_line):
            body = lines[row].rstrip("\r\n")
            for em in EXPR.finditer(body):
                expression = em.group(1)
                if UNTRUSTED.search(expression) or persona.lower() in ("pedantic", "auditor"):
                    matches.append((row, em, expression))
        if not matches:
            continue
        step_start_line = step_i if step_i is not None else i
        related_start = offsets[step_start_line] + lines[step_start_line].find(key.group(2) + ":")
        related_end_line = step_start_line + 1
        while related_end_line < len(lines):
            body = lines[related_end_line].rstrip("\r\n")
            ind = len(body) - len(body.lstrip())
            if body.strip() and (ind <= (len(lines[step_start_line]) - len(lines[step_start_line].lstrip()))):
                break
            related_end_line += 1
        related_end = offsets[related_end_line] if related_end_line < len(lines) else len(text)
        locations = []
        locations.append(finding_location(filename, "this step", route, text,
                                          related_start, related_end, kind="Hidden"))
        for row, em, expression in matches:
            # Source spans point at the expression body; the displayed feature
            # includes the surrounding command through the interpolation.
            mstart = offsets[row] + em.start(1)
            mend = offsets[row] + em.end(1)
            feature_start = offsets[row] + key.start(3)
            expr_route = route + ["run"]
            primary = finding_location(filename, "may expand into attacker-controllable code",
                expr_route, text, mstart, mend,
                feature_kind={"Subfeature": {"after": 6, "fragment": {"Raw": UNTRUSTED.search(expression).group(0) if UNTRUSTED.search(expression) else expression}}})
            primary["concrete"]["feature"] = text[feature_start:offsets[row] + em.end()]
            locations.append(primary)
            # Related key-only location indicates the run field containing code.
            key_start = offsets[i] + key.start(2)
            key_end = key_start + len(key.group(2))
            locations.append(finding_location(filename, f"this {key.group(2)} block", route + [key.group(2)],
                text, key_start, key_end, kind="Related", feature_kind="KeyOnly"))
        results.append(finding("template-injection", "code injection via template expansion",
                               "High", "High", persona, locations))
    return results

## `unsound-condition`

| Type     | Examples                | Introduced in | Works offline  | Auto-fixes available | Configurable |
|----------|-------------------------|---------------|----------------|--------------------| ---------------|
| Workflow, Action  | [unsound-condition.yml]   | v1.12.0      | ✅             | ✅                 | ❌  |

[unsound-condition.yml]: https://github.com/woodruffw/gha-hazmat/blob/main/.github/workflows/unsound-condition.yml

Detects conditions that are inadvertently always true despite containing
an expression that should control the evaluation.

A common source of these is an unintentional interaction
between multi-line YAML strings and fenced GitHub Actions expressions.
For example, the following condition always evaluates to `true`, despite
appearing to evaluate to `false`:

```yaml
if: |
  ${{ false }}
```

This happens because YAML's "block" scalars include a trailing newline
by default, which is left *outside* of the GitHub Actions expression.
This results in an expansion like `'false\n'` instead of `'false'`,
which GitHub Actions interprets as a truthy value.

### Remediation

There are two ways to remediate this:

* Avoid fenced expressions in `#!yaml if:` conditions. Instead, write
  the expression as a "bare" expression.

    This will still include the trailing newline, but it will be *inside*
    of the expression as seen from the GitHub Actions expression parser.

    !!! example

        === "Before :warning:"

            ```yaml title="unsound-condition.yml" hl_lines="6-7"
            jobs:
              build:
                runs-on: ubuntu-latest
                steps:
                  - run: echo "This will incorrectly always run"
                    if: |
                      ${{ false }}
            ```

        === "After :white_check_mark:"

            ```yaml title="unsound-condition.yml" hl_lines="6-7"
            jobs:
              build:
                runs-on: ubuntu-latest
                steps:
                  - run: echo "This will correctly not run"
                    if: |
                      false
            ```

* Use fenced expressions, but use a YAML block scalar that does not
  include a trailing newline. Either `|-` or `>-` is appropriate for
  this purpose.

    !!! example

        === "Before :warning:"

            ```yaml title="unsound-condition.yml" hl_lines="6-7"
            jobs:
              build:
                runs-on: ubuntu-latest
                steps:
                  - run: echo "This will incorrectly always run"
                    if: |
                      ${{ false }}
            ```

        === "After :white_check_mark:"

            ```yaml title="unsound-condition.yml" hl_lines="6-7"
            jobs:
              build:
                runs-on: ubuntu-latest
                steps:
                  - run: echo "This will correctly not run"
                    if: |-
                      ${{ false }}
            ```

+"""Detect fenced expressions in newline-terminated YAML conditions."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import os
+import re
+
+from finding import finding, finding_location
+
+
+def audit_unsound_condition(text: str, filename: str, persona: str = "regular") -> list[dict]:
+    lines = text.splitlines(keepends=True)
+    offsets, offset = [], 0
+    for line in lines:
+        offsets.append(offset)
+        offset += len(line.encode("utf-8"))
+    path = os.path.abspath(filename)
+    jobs = []
+    current = None
+    for i, raw in enumerate(lines):
+        line = raw.rstrip("\r\n")
+        if re.match(r"^  [^\s#][^:]*:\s*$", line):
+            m = re.match(r"^  (.*?):\s*$", line)
+            current = {"name": m.group(1).strip("'\""), "start": i, "steps": []}
+            jobs.append(current)
+        if current is not None and re.match(r"^\s{6}-\s+", line):
+            current["steps"].append(i)
+
+    findings = []
+    for ji, job in enumerate(jobs):
+        job_end_line = (jobs[ji+1]["start"] - 1) if ji+1 < len(jobs) else len(lines) - 1
+        if not lines:
+            continue
+        job_start = offsets[job["start"]]
+        job_end = offsets[job_end_line] + len(lines[job_end_line].rstrip("\r\n").encode("utf-8"))
+        for line_no in range(job["start"] + 1, job_end_line + 1):
+            raw = lines[line_no].rstrip("\r\n")
+            m = re.match(r"^(\s*)if\s*:\s*(\||>)\s*(?:#.*)?$", raw)
+            if not m:
+                continue
+            indent = len(m.group(1))
+            end_line = line_no
+            has_expression = False
+            for k in range(line_no + 1, job_end_line + 1):
+                body = lines[k].rstrip("\r\n")
+                if body.strip() and len(body) - len(body.lstrip()) <= indent:
+                    break
+                end_line = k
+                if "${{" in body and "}}" in body:
+                    has_expression = True
+            if not has_expression:
+                continue
+            condition_start = offsets[line_no] + len(raw[:len(m.group(1))].encode("utf-8"))
+            condition_end = offsets[end_line] + len(lines[end_line].rstrip("\r\n").encode("utf-8"))
+            step_starts = [s for s in job["steps"] if s < line_no]
+            if step_starts and len(raw) - len(raw.lstrip()) >= 8:
+                step_start = step_starts[-1]
+                siblings = [s for s in job["steps"] if s > step_start]
+                block_end_line = (siblings[0] - 1) if siblings else job_end_line
+                dash = re.match(r"^(\s*)-\s+", lines[step_start])
+                start_col = len(dash.group(1)) + 2 if dash else 0
+                hidden_start = offsets[step_start] + start_col
+                hidden_end = offsets[block_end_line] + len(lines[block_end_line].rstrip("\r\n").encode("utf-8"))
+                step_index = sum(1 for s in job["steps"] if s <= step_start) - 1
+                hidden_route = ["jobs", job["name"], "steps", step_index]
+                hidden_annotation = "this step"
+                route = hidden_route + ["if"]
+            else:
+                hidden_start, hidden_end = job_start, job_end
+                hidden_route = ["jobs", job["name"]]
+                hidden_annotation = "this job"
+                route = hidden_route + ["if"]
+            hidden = finding_location(path, hidden_annotation, hidden_route, text, hidden_start, hidden_end, kind="Hidden")
+            primary = finding_location(path, "condition always evaluates to true", route, text, condition_start, condition_end)
+            findings.append(finding("unsound-condition", "unsound conditional expression", "High", "High", persona.capitalize(), [hidden, primary]))
+    return findings
+
*** End Patch";

"""Self-hosted runner audit (available in auditor persona)."""
import re
from finding import finding, finding_location


def audit_self_hosted_runner(text: str, filename: str, persona: str = "Regular") -> list[dict]:
    if persona.lower() != "auditor":
        return []
    lines = text.splitlines(keepends=True)
    offsets, pos = [], 0
    for line in lines:
        offsets.append(pos); pos += len(line)
    jobs = []
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        m = re.match(r"^\s{2}([^\s#][^:]*):\s*(?:#.*)?$", line.rstrip("\r\n"))
        if m:
            jobs.append((i, m.group(1).strip().strip("'\"")))
    results = []
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        m = re.match(r"^(\s*)runs-on\s*:\s*(.*?)(?:\r?\n)?$", line, re.I)
        if not m or not re.search(r"(?:^|[\[ ,])self-hosted(?:$|[\], ])", m.group(2), re.I):
            continue
        parent = next(((j, name) for j, name in reversed(jobs) if j < i), None)
        if not parent:
            continue
        job_i, job = parent
        start = offsets[i] + len(m.group(1))
        end = offsets[i] + len(line.rstrip("\r\n"))
        loc = finding_location(filename, "self-hosted runner used here", ["jobs", job, "runs-on"],
                               text, start, end)
        loc["concrete"]["feature"] = line.rstrip("\r\n")
        results.append(finding("self-hosted-runner", "runs on a self-hosted runner", "Medium", "High",
                               persona.capitalize(), [loc]))
    return results

[protection rules]: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/deploy/configure-and-manage-deployments/manage-environments#creating-an-environment

Consequently, configuring secrets at the environment level ensures that they're
only exposed to jobs that meet the environment's protection rules, mitigating
the risk of secrets being exposed to untrusted code or compromised workflows.

!!! tip

    The `secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN` secret is a special case, and is not flagged
    by this audit. This is because the permissions of the `GITHUB_TOKEN`
    secret are entirely determined by the workflow and job-level permissions.

!!! note

    Starting with zizmor 1.24.0, these findings are only shown when running
    with the "auditor" [persona](./usage.md#using-personas), as fixing them
    requires careful consideration of GitHub's platform limitations. In
    particular, as of March 2026 environment secrets do not interact correctly
    with reusable workflows unless the caller workflow uses `secrets: inherit`,
    which is itself flagged by [secrets-inherit](./audits.md#secrets-inherit).
    
### Remediation

In general, secrets should be configured at the environment level, and only
the job or jobs that need a secret should use the corresponding environment.

!!! important

    zizmor will assume that referenced secrets are environment secrets if
    the job has an associated environment. zizmor cannot actually see
    where secrets are stored on GitHub's side.

    You **must** move your secrets into the environment's secrets (and remove
    them from the repo/org-wide secrets) in order for this to be effective.
    
!!! example

    === "Before :warning:"

        ```yaml title="secrets-outside-env.yml" hl_lines="7"
        jobs:
          deploy:
            runs-on: ubuntu-latest
            steps:
              - run: ./deploy.sh
                env:
                  API_KEY: ${{ secrets.API_KEY }}
        ```

    === "After :white_check_mark:"

        ```yaml title="secrets-outside-env.yml" hl_lines="4 8"
        jobs:
          deploy:
            runs-on: ubuntu-latest
            environment: production
            steps:
              - run: ./deploy.sh
                env:
                  API_KEY: ${{ secrets.API_KEY }}
        ```

### Configuration { #secrets-outside-env-configuration }

!!! tip

    `secrets-outside-env` is configurable in `v1.24.0` and later. 

#### `rules.secrets-outside-env.config.allow`

_Type_: `list`

The `secrets-outside-env` audit operates on an allowlist basis:

* Findings for secrets matching the allowlist will not be flagged by this audit.

    Intended use case: only allowing "special" secrets to be used outside environments,
    and forbidding everything else.

* The `GITHUB_TOKEN` secret is never flagged by this audit.

!!! example

    The following configuration would allow any usage of `CI_COVERAGE_TOKEN`
    and `NOT_VERY_SENSITIVE`, even outside of an environment.

    ```yaml title="zizmor.yml"
    rules:
      secrets-outside-env:
        config:
          allow:
            - CI_COVERAGE_TOKEN
            - NOT_VERY_SENSITIVE
    ```

+"""Flag non-token secrets referenced by jobs without an environment."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import os
+import re
+
+from finding import finding, finding_location
+
+
+_SECRET = re.compile(r"\$\{\{\s*secrets\.([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\s*\}\}")
+
+
+def audit_secrets_outside_env(text: str, filename: str, persona: str = "regular",
+                              allow: set[str] | None = None) -> list[dict]:
+    if persona.lower() != "auditor":
+        return []
+    lines = text.splitlines(keepends=True)
+    offsets, offset = [], 0
+    for line in lines:
+        offsets.append(offset)
+        offset += len(line.encode("utf-8"))
+    starts = []
+    for i, raw in enumerate(lines):
+        m = re.match(r"^  ([^\s#][^:]*):\s*(?:#.*)?$", raw.rstrip("\r\n"))
+        if m:
+            starts.append((i, m.group(1).strip("'\"")))
+    findings = []
+    for index, (start_line, job) in enumerate(starts):
+        end = offsets[starts[index+1][0]] if index + 1 < len(starts) else len(text.encode("utf-8"))
+        start = offsets[start_line]
+        block = text.encode("utf-8")[start:end].decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
+        if re.search(r"(?m)^\s{4}environment\s*:", block):
+            continue
+        key_col = len(lines[start_line]) - len(lines[start_line].lstrip()) + 2
+        name_start = offsets[start_line] + key_col
+        name_end = name_start + len(job.encode("utf-8"))
+        related = finding_location(os.path.abspath(filename), "this job", ["jobs", job], text,
+                                   name_start, name_end, kind="Related", feature_kind="KeyOnly")
+        for match in _SECRET.finditer(block):
+            secret = match.group(1)
+            if secret == "GITHUB_TOKEN" or (allow and secret in allow):
+                continue
+            before = block[:match.start(1)]
+            primary_start = start + len(before.encode("utf-8"))
+            primary_end = primary_start + len(secret.__class__("secrets." + secret).encode("utf-8"))
+            # Locate the full context name; the source span intentionally
+            # excludes the surrounding `${{ ... }}` delimiters.
+            primary_end = primary_start + len(("secrets." + secret).encode("utf-8"))
+            primary = finding_location(os.path.abspath(filename), "secret is accessed outside of a dedicated environment",
+                                       ["jobs", job], text, primary_start, primary_end)
+            findings.append(finding("secrets-outside-env", "secrets referenced without a dedicated environment",
+                                    "Medium", "High", "Auditor", [related, primary]))
+    return findings
+
*** End Patch";

"""Detect fenced expressions in newline-terminated YAML conditions."""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import re

from finding import finding, finding_location


def audit_unsound_condition(text: str, filename: str, persona: str = "regular") -> list[dict]:
    lines = text.splitlines(keepends=True)
    offsets, offset = [], 0
    for line in lines:
        offsets.append(offset)
        offset += len(line.encode("utf-8"))
    path = os.path.abspath(filename)
    jobs = []
    current = None
    for i, raw in enumerate(lines):
        line = raw.rstrip("\r\n")
        if re.match(r"^  [^\s#][^:]*:\s*$", line):
            m = re.match(r"^  (.*?):\s*$", line)
            current = {"name": m.group(1).strip("'\""), "start": i, "steps": []}
            jobs.append(current)
        if current is not None and re.match(r"^\s{6}-\s+", line):
            current["steps"].append(i)

    findings = []
    for ji, job in enumerate(jobs):
        job_end_line = (jobs[ji+1]["start"] - 1) if ji+1 < len(jobs) else len(lines) - 1
        if not lines:
            continue
        job_start = offsets[job["start"]]
        job_end = (offsets[job_end_line] + len(lines[job_end_line].rstrip("\r\n").encode("utf-8"))
                   if ji+1 < len(jobs) else len(text.encode("utf-8")))
        for line_no in range(job["start"] + 1, job_end_line + 1):
            raw = lines[line_no].rstrip("\r\n")
            m = re.match(r"^(\s*)if\s*:\s*([|>][+-]?)\s*(?:#.*)?$", raw)
            if not m:
                continue
            if m.group(2).endswith("-"):
                continue
            indent = len(m.group(1))
            end_line = line_no
            has_expression = False
            for k in range(line_no + 1, job_end_line + 1):
                body = lines[k].rstrip("\r\n")
                if body.strip() and len(body) - len(body.lstrip()) <= indent:
                    break
                end_line = k
                if "${{" in body and "}}" in body:
                    has_expression = True
            if not has_expression:
                continue
            condition_start = offsets[line_no] + len(raw[:len(m.group(1))].encode("utf-8"))
            condition_end = offsets[end_line] + len(lines[end_line].rstrip("\r\n").encode("utf-8"))
            step_starts = [s for s in job["steps"] if s < line_no]
            if step_starts and len(raw) - len(raw.lstrip()) >= 8:
                step_start = step_starts[-1]
                siblings = [s for s in job["steps"] if s > step_start]
                block_end_line = (siblings[0] - 1) if siblings else job_end_line
                dash = re.match(r"^(\s*)-\s+", lines[step_start])
                start_col = len(dash.group(1)) + 2 if dash else 0
                hidden_start = offsets[step_start] + start_col
                hidden_end = offsets[block_end_line] + len(lines[block_end_line].rstrip("\r\n").encode("utf-8"))
                step_index = sum(1 for s in job["steps"] if s <= step_start) - 1
                hidden_route = ["jobs", job["name"], "steps", step_index]
                hidden_annotation = "this step"
                route = hidden_route + ["if"]
            else:
                hidden_start, hidden_end = job_start, job_end
                hidden_route = ["jobs", job["name"]]
                hidden_annotation = "this job"
                route = hidden_route + ["if"]
            hidden = finding_location(path, hidden_annotation, hidden_route, text, hidden_start, hidden_end, kind="Hidden")
            primary = finding_location(path, "condition always evaluates to true", route, text, condition_start, condition_end)
            findings.append(finding("unsound-condition", "unsound conditional expression", "High", "High", persona.capitalize(), [hidden, primary]))
    return findings

"""Source-based template injection audit for GitHub Actions code fields."""
import re
from finding import finding, finding_location

UNTRUSTED = re.compile(r"github\.event\.(?:issue\.(?:title|body)|pull_request\.(?:title|body)|comment\.(?:body)|review\.(?:body)|discussion\.(?:title|body))", re.I)
EXPR = re.compile(r"\$\{\{\s*(.*?)\s*\}\}")


def audit_template_injection(text: str, filename: str, persona: str = "Regular") -> list[dict]:
    lines = text.splitlines(keepends=True)
    offsets, off = [], 0
    for line in lines:
        offsets.append(off); off += len(line)
    jobs = []
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        jm = re.match(r"^\s{2}([^\s#][^:]*):\s*(?:#.*)?$", line.rstrip("\r\n"))
        if jm:
            jobs.append((i, jm.group(1).strip().strip("'\"")))
    results = []
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        # run: and script-like code contexts are analyzed; inline expressions
        # in env/with values do not execute as code directly.
        key = re.match(r"^(\s*)(?:-\s*)?(run|script|inlineScript)\s*:\s*(.*?)(?:\r?\n)?$", line, re.I)
        if not key:
            continue
        indent = len(key.group(1))
        jobpair = next(((n, name) for n, name in reversed(jobs) if n < i), None)
        if not jobpair:
            continue
        job_i, job = jobpair
        step_i = next((k for k in range(i, job_i, -1) if re.match(r"^\s{6}-\s+", lines[k])), None)
        job_route = ["jobs", job]
        if step_i is not None:
            step_indent = len(lines[step_i]) - len(lines[step_i].lstrip())
            index = sum(1 for k in range(job_i + 1, step_i + 1)
                        if re.match(r"^\s{%d}-\s+" % step_indent, lines[k])) - 1
            route = job_route + ["steps", index]
        else:
            route = job_route
        code_start_line = i
        code_end_line = i + 1
        if key.group(3).strip() in ("|", ">", "|-", ">-") or not key.group(3).strip():
            while code_end_line < len(lines):
                s = lines[code_end_line].rstrip("\r\n")
                if s.strip() and len(s) - len(s.lstrip()) <= indent:
                    break
                code_end_line += 1
        code_start = offsets[code_start_line] + key.start(2)
        code_end = offsets[code_end_line] if code_end_line < len(lines) else len(text)
        # Find expressions in source lines inside the code field.
        matches = []
        for row in range(i, code_end_line):
            body = lines[row].rstrip("\r\n")
            for em in EXPR.finditer(body):
                expression = em.group(1)
                if UNTRUSTED.search(expression) or persona.lower() in ("pedantic", "auditor"):
                    matches.append((row, em, expression))
        if not matches:
            continue
        step_start_line = step_i if step_i is not None else i
        dash_match = re.match(r"^(\s*)-\s+", lines[step_start_line])
        related_start = offsets[step_start_line] + len(dash_match.group(1)) + 2 if dash_match else offsets[i] + lines[i].find(key.group(2) + ":")
        related_end_line = step_start_line + 1
        step_indent = len(dash_match.group(1)) if dash_match else indent
        while related_end_line < len(lines):
            body = lines[related_end_line].rstrip("\r\n")
            ind = len(body) - len(body.lstrip())
            if body.strip() and (ind <= step_indent or re.match(r"^\s{%d}-\s+" % step_indent, lines[related_end_line])):
                break
            related_end_line += 1
        related_end = offsets[related_end_line] if related_end_line < len(lines) else len(text)
        for row, em, expression in matches:
            locations = [finding_location(filename, "this step", route, text,
                                          related_start, related_end, kind="Hidden")]
            # Source spans point at the expression body; the displayed feature
            # includes the surrounding command through the interpolation.
            mstart = offsets[row] + em.start(1)
            mend = offsets[row] + em.end(1)
            first_row, first_em, _ = matches[0]
            body = lines[row].rstrip("\r\n")
            quoted = em.end() < len(body) and body[em.end()] in "'\""
            after = 6 + mstart - (offsets[first_row] + first_em.start(1)) + int(quoted)
            feature_start = offsets[i] + key.start(3)
            feature_end = code_end - 1 if code_end > feature_start and text[code_end - 1:code_end] == "\n" else code_end
            expr_route = route + ["run"]
            locations = [finding_location(filename, "this step", route, text,
                                          related_start, related_end, kind="Hidden")]
            primary = finding_location(filename, "may expand into attacker-controllable code",
                expr_route, text, mstart, mend,
                feature_kind={"Subfeature": {"after": after, "fragment": {"Raw": UNTRUSTED.search(expression).group(0) if UNTRUSTED.search(expression) else expression}}})
            primary["concrete"]["feature"] = text[feature_start:feature_end]
            locations.append(primary)
            # Related key-only location indicates the run field containing code.
            key_start = offsets[i] + key.start(2)
            key_end = key_start + len(key.group(2))
            locations.append(finding_location(filename, f"this {key.group(2)} block", route + [key.group(2)],
                text, key_start, key_end, kind="Related", feature_kind="KeyOnly"))
            results.append(finding("template-injection", "code injection via template expansion",
                                   "High", "High", persona, locations))
    return results

+            start = path if path.is_dir() else path.parent
+            if start.name == "workflows" and start.parent.name == ".github":
